title: Perfect-algebra coinduction is tensor with its algebra-valued dual
statement:
Let $R\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Work in the ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], or equivalently on one-object ringed sites, with derived Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Assume that $B[0]$ is perfect over $R$, that is, isomorphic in $D(R)$ to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Write $C_B(K)\in D(B)$ for derived coinduction: if $K\to I$ is a K-injective resolution of $R$-complexes, it is represented by $\operatorname{Hom}_R(B,I)$ with $(b\cdot h)(b')=h(b'b)$. Put $D_B=C_B(R[0])$. There is a natural isomorphism in $D(B)$
$$K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D_B\xrightarrow{\sim}C_B(K)\qquad(K\in D(R)),$$
where tensor with the $B$-complex $D_B$ is [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. The comparison is adjoint to the map from the scalar restriction of $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D_B$ to $K$ obtained by tensoring $K$ with the evaluation counit $D_B\to R[0]$, $h\mapsto h(1)$. Thus its scalar restriction is the usual perfect-complex evaluation comparison $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(B,R)\to R\operatorname{Hom}_R(B,K)$. No boundedness of $K$, flatness of $B$ over $R$, or Noetherianity is required.

source.place: Tag 0BZE (lemma-RHom-is-tensor-special), with the evaluation-normalized comparison of trivial duality, Tags 0A70 and 0A71.

proof.text: For the given ring map, apply [lem-trf-coinduction-tensor-comparison-model]. It supplies a canonical natural transformation $\sigma_K:K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D_B\to C_B(K)$ with exactly the tensor-counit adjunct required here. Choose a K-flat representative $F$ of $K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the small one-object site, and K-injective resolutions $R[0]\to J$ and $q:F\otimes_RJ\to I$ by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Using its specified identification $QI\cong K$, the model lemma identifies the source with $F\otimes_R\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(B[0],J)$, the target with $\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(B[0],I)$, and $\sigma_K$ with the localization of the $B$-linear chain map $t(f\otimes h)(b)=q(f\otimes h(b))$. It also identifies its scalar restriction with ordinary Hom/tensor evaluation.

source.place: Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint) and 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext), explicit tensor-counit adjunct on K-flat and K-injective representatives.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-perfect-source-evaluation-quasi-isomorphism] to $M=B[0]$ and the complexes $F,J,I,q$ just chosen. Its perfect-source hypothesis is precisely the assumption on $B[0]$: $F$ is K-flat, $J,I$ are K-injective, and $q:F\otimes_RJ\to I$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the chosen resolutions. Its specified map is exactly the scalar restriction of $t$, so $U(\sigma_K)$ is an isomorphism in $D(R)$. Conservativity of scalar restriction in [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] makes $\sigma_K$ an isomorphism in $D(B)$. The naturality, independence of representatives, tensor-counit normalization and underlying evaluation identification supplied in the first step therefore give the claimed natural isomorphism with every stated clause. Neither extracted lemma imposes any extra boundedness, flatness or Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0ATK (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism), case (1); explicit projective-source comparison of K-flat/K-injective models.
